description.ncbi_summary: This gene encodes a mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate in the presence of guanosine triphosphate (GTP). A cytosolic form of this protein is encoded by a different gene and is the key enzyme of gluconeogenesis in the liver. Alternatively spliced transcript variants have been described. [provided by RefSeq, Apr 2014].

uniprot_function.text: Mitochondrial phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase that catalyzes the conversion of oxaloacetate (OAA) to phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP), the rate-limiting step in the metabolic pathway that produces glucose from lactate and other precursors derived from the citric acid cycle (PubMed:28955899). Can play an active role in glyceroneogenesis and gluconeogenesis (PubMed:28955899). In lipogenic cells such as adipocytes, it generates PEP via the mitochondrial pyruvate-to-PEP bypass, driving the PEP flux required for cytosolic glycerol 3-phosphate and triglyceride synthesis (By similarity). Also acts as a serine/threonine-protein kinase: phosphorylates and activates ACSL4, thereby promoting ferroptosis (PubMed:38720107).
